swe_bench_milestones.date_clarification: 2023-10-10 is the arXiv preprint date for the original SWE-bench benchmark (Jimenez et al.); Claude 2 model was released on 2023-07-11.
swe_bench_milestones.notes: Original benchmark launch. Evaluated across 2,294 full GitHub issues. Reported 4.2% was an unverified secondary composite or Lite subset; 1.96% is the verified benchmark baseline.

swe_bench_milestones.date_clarification: 2024-08-13 is the official OpenAI/Princeton SWE-bench Verified launch date; Claude 3.5 Sonnet was released on 2024-06-20.
swe_bench_milestones.notes: Top launch baseline reported in OpenAI/Princeton launch announcement (168/500 tasks = 33.6% using SWE-agent scaffold; GPT-4o scored 33.2% with open scaffold in that evaluation).

swe_bench_milestones.date_clarification: 2024-09-02 is the revision date of the Agentless paper (arXiv:2407.01489v2) evaluating on SWE-bench Verified; underlying model GPT-4o was released on 2024-05-13.
swe_bench_milestones.notes: Evaluated on the 500-task SWE-bench Verified benchmark following its August 2024 release. Solved 194/500 tasks (38.8%) using GPT-4o with a two-phase localized edit scaffold without autonomous tool-use loops.

swe_bench_milestones.date_clarification: 2025-02-24 is the public announcement date of Anthropic's Claude 3.7 Sonnet release and evaluation report. The underlying model snapshot identifier is claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219 (reflecting Anthropic's internal build date of 2025-02-19).
swe_bench_milestones.evaluation_method: Pass@1 average across repeated evaluation trials
swe_bench_milestones.notes: Evaluated on 489 tasks due to 11 infrastructure-incompatible tasks excluded from the 500-task set. Expected resolved tasks (311.5) reflects Pass@1 average across evaluation runs.

swe_bench_milestones.date_clarification: 2025-02-24 is the public announcement date of Anthropic's high-compute test-time scaling evaluation report. The underlying model snapshot identifier is claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219 (reflecting Anthropic's internal build date of 2025-02-19).
swe_bench_milestones.scaffold: Anthropic Custom High-Compute Scaffold (Parallel Thinking & Tool Search)
swe_bench_milestones.evaluation_method: Pass@1 average across repeated evaluation trials with parallel test-time compute
swe_bench_milestones.notes: Employs test-time compute with parallel thinking. Evaluated on 489 tasks (11 tasks excluded due to environment incompatibilities). Expected resolved tasks (343.8) reflects Pass@1 average across evaluation runs.

stanford_adp_early_career_employment_res.citation: Brynjolfsson, Chandar, & Chen (Stanford Digital Economy Lab, 2025; rev. 2026)
stanford_adp_early_career_employment_res.paper_title: Canaries in the Coal Mine: Six Facts About the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence
stanford_adp_early_career_employment_res.dataset: ADP payroll records covering millions of US private-sector employees
stanford_adp_early_career_employment_res.core_finding: Employment among early-career workers (ages 22-25) in AI-exposed occupations was 19% below the trajectory it would have followed had it kept pace with less-exposed peers.
critical_caveats: The finding is descriptive of relative US private-sector employment trajectories among young workers in AI-exposed occupations, not causal proof that AI caused a decline specifically in software-developer employment.
The authors report no evidence of widespread, economy-wide job displacement.
The study evaluates US domestic payrolls and does not represent a direct measurement of entry-level vacancy shares in Pakistan or other offshore tech ecosystems.

pakistan_industry_benchmarks_2025_2026.source_report: P@SHA Skills Survey 2025 (P@SHA Research & Talent Committee)
pakistan_industry_benchmarks_2025_2026.survey_scope: Sample of surveyed participating P@SHA member enterprises (representing organized software export and IT service firms; does not represent a national census)
pakistan_industry_benchmarks_2025_2026.national_graduate_source: P@SHA institutional estimate across national Higher Education Institutions (HEIs)
pakistan_industry_benchmarks_2025_2026.scope_distinction_note: The 47,393 hires and 13,350 fresh graduate hires apply specifically to participating P@SHA member firms. The ratio of 13,350 fresh hires to 72,952 annual national graduates should NOT be interpreted as a national graduate employment rate, as graduates also enter non-member software houses, freelance contracting, domestic banking/telecom IT, and public-sector organizations.
pakistan_industry_benchmarks_2025_2026.cagr_derivation: Calculated from FY20 audited ($1.440B) to FY26 reported outturn ($4.600B): ((4.600 / 1.440)^(1/6) - 1) * 100 = 21.36% (~21.4%)

author_qualitative_skills_rubric.status: Author-Assigned Qualitative Evaluation (Reasoned Strategic Stance, Not Statistical Market Proof)
author_qualitative_skills_rubric.formula_description: Final Score = round((100 - Automation_Exposure) * 0.35 + Verification_Necessity * 0.40 + Screening_Rigor * 0.25)

skills_evaluations.justification: Heavily commoditized by LLMs. Autocompletion and agentic code synthesis generate standard boilerplate in seconds; minimal hiring differentiation for candidates possessing only syntax ability.
Contracting relative to automated test frameworks and synthetic test harnesses. Manual UI clicking provides lower leverage and compensation compared to automated QA engineering.

skills_evaluations.skill_domain: Backend Systems & API Architecture (Python / FastAPI + PostgreSQL)
skills_evaluations.justification: High-leverage core competency. Relational schema normalization, database indexing, ACID transactions, connection pooling, and REST API design with worker threadpool concurrency remain fundamental enterprise requirements.
The Verification Bottleneck. In an environment where code generation is accelerated, the primary human engineering constraint is verifying business correctness and integration integrity.

skills_evaluations.skill_domain: AI Integration & Practical Orchestration (APIs, Embeddings, RAG)
skills_evaluations.justification: Rapidly growing enterprise capability. Building applications that connect frontier models, structured Pydantic outputs, vector embeddings, and fallback mechanisms into reliable services.

skills_evaluations.skill_domain: Core Computer Science Fundamentals (DSA, Systems Design)
skills_evaluations.justification: Uncompromised screening standard across tier-1 software companies. Essential for evaluating algorithmic complexity, resource constraints, and performance tuning.
